summary: Duloxetine is an SNRI used for major depression, generalized anxiety disorder, diabetic neuropathic pain, fibromyalgia, and chronic musculoskeletal pain. It carries a boxed warning for suicidality in pediatric and young adult patients. It should be avoided in hepatic impairment, severe renal impairment, and significant alcohol use, and it can raise blood pressure and cause a discontinuation syndrome.
indications: Generalized anxiety disorder (adults and children >=7 years)

dosage.d: Start 40 mg/day (20 mg twice daily) to 60 mg/day; target 60 mg/day
dosage.n: Maximum 120 mg/day (no added benefit shown above 60 mg)

admin: Take once daily, with or without food

moa: Potent and balanced inhibitor of serotonin (5-HT) and norepinephrine reuptake, with weak effect on dopamine reuptake. Increasing serotonergic and noradrenergic neurotransmission in the CNS underlies both its antidepressant/anxiolytic and analgesic (descending pain pathway) effects.

absolute: Concurrent MAO inhibitors (or within 14 days; wait 5 days after stopping duloxetine before an MAOI)

preg: Use only if the potential benefit justifies the risk. Use late in the third trimester may cause neonatal complications (respiratory distress, feeding difficulty, irritability) and there may be a small increased risk of postpartum hemorrhage.
lact: Excreted into breast milk (about 0.1% of maternal dose reaches the infant). Use with caution; monitor the breastfed infant for sedation and poor feeding.
renal: Avoid in severe renal impairment (CrCl <30 mL/min) and end-stage renal disease, as the active metabolite accumulates.
hepatic: Avoid in patients with any hepatic impairment or substantial alcohol use due to the risk of hepatotoxicity and increased drug exposure.

major: Other serotonergic drugs (triptans, tramadol, linezolid, methylene blue)
Potent CYP1A2 inhibitors (fluvoxamine, ciprofloxacin - markedly raise duloxetine levels)
moderate: CYP2D6 substrates (TCAs, metoprolol, risperidone - raised levels)
minor: Smoking (reduces duloxetine exposure via CYP1A2 induction)
interactions.alcohol: Avoid - increased risk of liver injury
interactions.diagnostics: Monitor liver enzymes; may affect bleeding parameters

monitoring: Suicidality and mood, especially early and after dose changes
Liver function tests if symptoms or risk factors
Signs of serotonin syndrome and bleeding

missed: Take the missed dose as soon as remembered; if it is almost time for the next dose, skip it and continue the schedule. Do not double up.
overdose: Overdose (alone or with other drugs) may cause serotonin syndrome, drowsiness, vomiting, tachycardia, hypertension or hypotension, seizures, and (rarely) coma; fatalities have occurred, often with mixed ingestions. Management is supportive with airway protection, ECG/cardiac monitoring, and treatment of serotonin syndrome; activated charcoal may help if early. Dialysis is not useful (high protein binding). No specific antidote.
